text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Start allopurinol 100 mg daily and raise it by 100 mg every 2 to 5 weeks until serum urate is below 6 mg/dL; HLA-B*58:01 testing is not indicated, because he is not of Southeast Asian or African ancestry
  • Colchicine 0.6 mg daily for three to six months as flare prophylaxis; treat flares with a short prednisone course or extra colchicine, and avoid NSAIDs because of chronic kidney disease
  • Replace hydrochlorothiazide with losartan, which lowers blood pressure and slightly lowers urate; check potassium and creatinine 2 to 4 weeks after starting
  • Urology referral to confirm and remove the bladder stone, look for bladder outlet obstruction and other causes of hematuria, and advise on stone prevention
  • Uric acid stone prevention: fluids for a urine output of at least 2.5 L a day, potassium citrate to a urine pH of 6.0 to 6.5, stone analysis, and a 24-hour urine collection
  • CMID kidney and blood pressure monitoring: blood pressure every visit; eGFR and urine albumin yearly at G3a A1; calcium, phosphate, and PTH at baseline; hemoglobin and the kidney failure risk equation yearly; statin for age over 50 with eGFR below 60; medication review for NSAIDs every visit
  • Limit alcohol, especially beer and spirits, and purine-rich meat, organ meat, and shellfish; avoid sugar-sweetened drinks; aim for gradual weight loss and daily walking

resource.title: Benjamin Franklin synthetic care plan
resource.description: Manage recurrent gout in a 76-year-old man with stage 3a chronic kidney disease by the 2020 ACR treat-to-target approach (allopurinol started low and titrated to a serum urate below 6 mg/dL, colchicine prophylaxis, a thiazide replaced by losartan), and evaluate a bladder stone with imaging, cystoscopy, and flow studies, treating its outlet-obstruction cause and preventing uric acid stones with fluids, urinary alkalinization, and metabolic testing, while following the CMID kidney, blood pressure, and prostate schedules.
